chapter.neropower.reactor_log.title: Reactor Log
quest.neropower.reactor_log.cells.title: Cells
quest.neropower.reactor_log.cells.desc: A basic battery cell and a bank controller: the start of a power reserve you can grow.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.tiered_stora: Advanced and elite cells. Your bank now holds far more than a handful of basic cells could.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.gradient.des: A Stirling generator and a radioisotope generator, both making power from a difference in temperature.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.pellets.desc: Uranium pellets on hand and an isotope pellet made from them: the fuel for the nuclear side of NeroPower.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.beamed.title: Beamed
quest.neropower.reactor_log.beamed.desc: A transmitter, a receiver and a relay. Power can now cross the distance without a single cable.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.orbital.desc: An orbital receiver, built to catch power beamed down from far above.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.fission_buil: Core, control rod assembly, casing, control rods and fuel rods. Everything a fission reactor needs is ready.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.first_burn.d: A spent fuel rod: proof your reactor has run a full fuel cycle.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.decay_heat.d: A spent isotope pellet, its decay heat fully turned into power.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.closing_the_: Reprocessed pellets recovered from used fuel. What came out of the reactor goes back into it.
Your formed reactor burned fuel for the first time. From here on the fuel cycle is yours to manage.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.turbine_spin: Your Steam Turbine reached rated speed and delivered power. Steam now does the work the core used to do directly.
Breeder Blankets in a running reactor kindled their first pellet. The reactor now makes part of its own fuel.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.first_vitrif: Your Vitrifier sealed waste into its first Vitrified Waste log. Keep it behind shielding.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.smes_charged: A formed SMES storage ring holds its full charge. Keep the cryo coolant flowing, or it warms and quenches.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.beam_link.de: Link a beam transmitter to a target you may use. Power now crosses the gap on a beam you aimed.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.power_bank.d: Grow a battery bank until its pooled capacity reaches the server's milestone. A reserve that outlasts the night.
quest.neropower.reactor_log.world_first_: Somewhere in this world a fission reactor has burned fuel for the first time. A shared entry in the reactor log.

gui.neropower.power_guide.title: Power Guide
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.steam_mod: Set a Reactor Steam Port into the reactor's wall, feed it water (a pipe, or a tank or condenser touching it) and switch the Fission Core to steam mode. All of a reactor's ports share its tanks. The core now makes steam instead of power. If the water runs out or the steam has nowhere to go, the heat stays in the core. Next: the Turbine Helm.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.turbine_h: A steam turbine is a tube of Turbine Shroud, 5 by 5 across and 4 to 16 blocks long, with the Turbine Helm in the centre of one end. The Helm's screen shows the rotor speed and, when the turbine stops, why. Next: the Turbine Spindle.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.turbine_s: Run Turbine Spindles down the middle of the tube. Each slice around the spindle is one of two kinds: an open ring with a Vane Set on the spindle, or a ring of eight Turbine Stators. You need at least one of each. Next: Vane Sets.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.vane_sets: Right-click a Turbine Spindle with a Vane Set to mount it. A steel slice passes 40 mB of steam a tick at 55% efficiency, cindersteel 70 mB at 65%, superconducting 110 mB at 75%. More vaned slices pass more steam. Next: Turbine Stators.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.turbine_s: Stators turn spin into power. Wind each one by right-clicking it with a NeroTech coil: a Nero Coil gives 15 NE/t, and the two better coil tiers give 40 and 100. A ring of eight makes 120, 320 or 800 NE/t. Next: Turbine Steam Ports.

Put 1 to 8 Turbine Steam Ports in the side walls and click each with an empty hand to set it. Inlet takes steam in, exhaust sends used steam to a Steam Condenser, vent blows it into the air. Venting keeps only 60% of the power. Next: spin-up and overspeed.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.rotor_spe: The rotor takes 30 seconds to reach its rated 1,800 rpm and 90 seconds to coast down; power scales with speed. If the stators or the buffer cannot take the power, it overspeeds and trips at 2,100 rpm. Reset it at the Helm below 600 rpm. A Governor Module prevents that. Next: the Steam Condenser.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.condenser: Turns exhaust steam back into water, one for one. Put a Reactor Steam Port (or a tank) against it and the water goes back by itself, so the loop needs no pipes and never needs topping up. On Earth-like air it handles 200 mB a tick. In a vacuum it needs NeroTech Radiators beside it (30 mB a tick each) or cryo coolant. Next: what steam is worth.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.steam_yie: With a turbine and a condenser, a rod gives 1.1 times its direct-mode power on steel vanes, 1.3 on cindersteel and 1.5 on superconducting. Vent the exhaust and steam always loses. Cryo coolant in a Reactor Steam Port cools the core and widens its safe band. Next: the fuel lines.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.standard_: Uranium Pellets make Fuel Rods, and Fuel Rods go in the Fission Core. A rod gives the most power when fresh and less as it burns up. Pull rods only when they are spent: a partly used rod comes out as a Hot Spent Fuel Rod. Next: moderators.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.moderator: A Graphite Moderator inside the reactor raises output and heat by 1% for every open space it touches, up to 40% in all. Layout matters: leave gaps beside them. A Moderator Tank counts double. Next: control rods.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.reactor_c: A Control Rod Assembly lowers output and heat by 15%; a Europium Control Rod Assembly by 25%. A Reactor Control Computer in the wall gives redstone and comparator signals and can SCRAM the reactor by itself. The largest reactor, 7 blocks a side, needs one. Next: Pallurite.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.pallurite: The second fuel line starts here. A NeroTech Centrifuge spins certain Nerospace crystals, or a meteor core, into two Pallurite Dust. Without Nerospace, 8 tuff and 4 glowstone dust give one, at about four times the power and time. Two dust and an iron nugget make a Pallurite Pellet. Next: the Breeder Blanket.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.breeder_b: Build Breeder Blankets into the reactor and put Pallurite Pellets in the core's blanket slot. While the reactor runs they become Kindled Pellets: about 30 minutes each with one blanket at full output, faster with more, up to 8. Each blanket costs 5% of output and heat. Next: the Braided Fuel Rod.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.braided_f: Two Kindled Pellets, a Reprocessed Pellet and two cindersteel rods make a Braided Fuel Rod. It gives 1.4 times a Fuel Rod's power and lasts a quarter longer. It only works when the reactor's Moderator Tanks touch at least four open spaces between them, so build 5 or 7 blocks a side. Next: the Fuel Economizer.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.fuel_econ: A Fission Core upgrade. Rods burn up a quarter slower and give a tenth less power, so each rod gives about 20% more over its life. Next: waste, starting with the Hot Spent Fuel Rod.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.hot_spent: A burnt-out rod leaves the reactor as a Hot Spent Fuel Rod. It is too hot to reprocess, and it gives off radiation if you drop it. It cools in one place only. Next: the Spent Fuel Rack.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.spent_fue: Place the rack under water and put up to four hot rods in it. Each rod adds heat; each water source on the rack's top or sides carries one rod's heat away. Kept calm, a rod becomes a Spent Fuel Rod in about 17 minutes. An overheated rack stops cooling, and a failed one releases radiation. Next: reprocessing.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.reprocess: A NeroTech Centrifuge turns a Spent Fuel Rod into two Reprocessed Pellets and one Fission Residue. A Chemical Processor gives one pellet and no residue. Two Reprocessed Pellets make a Uranium Pellet, and every Braided Fuel Rod needs one. Next: Fission Residue.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.fission_r: Residue is waste, but not a dead end. A Centrifuge turns four Fission Residue into a Beta Capsule and hands two residue back. Whatever you do not use must be stored or vitrified. Next: the Betavoltaic Cell.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.betavolta: A half-height cell that turns one Beta Capsule into a steady 4 NE/t for about 30 in-game days. The output never fades; it stops when the capsule is spent. A capsule is sealed in once inserted. Take out the Spent Beta Capsule and vitrify it. Next: the Vitrifier.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.vitrifier: Melts one piece of final waste (Fission Residue, a Spent Beta Capsule or a Spent Isotope Pellet) with two sand into Vitrified Waste. Each one costs 8,000 NE and makes nothing useful: this is how waste leaves your base for good. Vitrified Waste is inert. Next: the Dry Cask.
A 27-slot store for Spent Fuel Rods, Fission Residue and Vitrified Waste. Rods and residue give off a little heat, and radiation through any face not covered by shielding. Cover all six faces and the cask gives off nothing. Next: storage, starting with Battery Cells.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.battery_c: Basic, Advanced and Elite Battery Cells hold 500,000, 2 million and 8 million NE. Cells joined face to face beside a Battery Bank Controller become one bank that fills and empties as a single store. Each cell has a slot that charges a Power Cell. Next: the Surge Bank.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.surge_ban: Holds only 200,000 NE but moves 50,000 NE a tick. Next to a Battery Bank it joins as the fast tier: it fills first and empties first, soaking up turbine spin-up and beam bursts. Alone, it is a small, fast store. Next: the Momentum Wheel.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.momentum_: Stores up to 2 million NE as spin. Friction takes 0.2% of its charge every second, so use it to smooth short dips, not to hold power for days. It never joins a bank. Next: the Storage Ring.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.storage_r: The largest store there is. Build a hollow square of Storage Ring Coils, 5 to 15 blocks a side and one layer high, with the Storage Ring Controller in the middle of one side. Every coil adds 50 million NE. Next: keeping the ring cold.

Keep the ring's tank fed with cryo coolant. Starved, the coils warm and its I/O halves. At the top it quenches: it loses half its charge and goes offline for at least a minute, until it is cold again. By default nothing is damaged. Next: Power Cells.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.power_cel: Portable energy. Basic, Advanced and Elite Power Cells hold 250,000, 1 million and 4 million NE. Make them in a NeroTech Reaction Vat with sulfuric acid. Charge them in a Battery Cell or Surge Bank slot, or near an Induction Charger. Next: beam grids, starting with the Beam Transmitter.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.beam_tran: A Beam Transmitter sends power in a straight line to a Beam Receiver up to 128 blocks away. Link them with NeroTech's Configurator: click the transmitter, then the receiver. The beam loses about 0.3% per block, stops at any solid block and hurts anything standing in it. Next: the Beam Relay.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.beam_rela: Receives a beam and passes it on, to bend around terrain or reach past the range. Link each hop with the Configurator; a chain can be 8 hops long. To take power out of a relay, open one of its faces in its screen. Next: the Beam Splitter.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.beam_spli: Takes one beam and shares it over up to four. It needs a NeroTech focus lens: quartz loses 5%, glacite 3%, ember 2% and void 1%. Link it to receivers with the Configurator, then set each link's share in its screen. What you leave unshared stays in its buffer. Next: the Phased Array Emitter.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.phased_ar: A long-range transmitter. It reaches 384 blocks, loses a third as much over distance as a Beam Transmitter and serves up to four receivers in turn, one each pass. Reorder its targets in its screen. Next: the Beam Alignment Scope.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.beam_alig: Hold it and look at any block that sends a beam to see the beam's line of sight and what is in the way. Reach for it when a screen says the beam is blocked. Next: grid tools, starting with the Circuit Breaker.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.circuit_b: Put it in a line, back to the supply and front to the load, and set a limit; it starts at 10,000 NE/t. Load above 60% of the limit warns, and load at the limit for a moment trips it open. Nothing is damaged. Reset it from its screen, by right-clicking its front, or with a redstone pulse. Next: the Load Bank.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.load_bank: Burns power on purpose, up to 20,000 NE/t, and turns it into heat. Use it to test a supply or soak up a surplus. A Stirling Generator on it gets back less than half. Next: the Power Monitor.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.power_mon: Mount it on a store or a machine to see its last minute of power in, power out and charge. A comparator reads how full the store is. Next: radiation, starting with where it comes from.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.radiation: A reactor or Spent Fuel Rack that fails, a Dry Cask holding rods or residue, and rods or residue dropped on the ground all contaminate the chunk they are in. Contamination is measured in pall (pl). It fades by itself over a few hours, never spreads to the next chunk and never harms blocks. Next: what it does to you.

From 200 pl you are weakened, from 500 pl also hungry, and from 800 pl you take damage. Each piece of shielding armour you wear, such as a Nerospace suit piece with a rad lining, takes a quarter off. A full set makes you immune. Next: shielding.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.shielding: Put Shielding Blocks or Shielding Glass against a waste store: every face you cover stops leaking. A Dry Cask boxed in on all six sides gives off nothing, and the glass lets you see in. Shielding does not hold back the burst from a failure. Next: the Geiger Counter.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.geiger_co: Hold it to see the contamination of your chunk and the eight around it, and how many radiation sources are within 16 blocks. It clicks faster the hotter the ground. Next: the Dosimeter Badge.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.dosimeter: Carry it, and it adds up the radiation it has been in. The reading is kept on the badge and nowhere else. Craft the badge by itself to reset it. Next: Decontaminant.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.decontami: Use it on any block to clean 250 pl from that chunk. A NeroTech Reaction Vat makes four at a time from clay, bone meal and sulfuric acid. Next: the radiation setting.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.radiation: Radiation is a server setting called radiationMode. Left on auto, it is on in single-player and LAN worlds and off on a dedicated server until the operator turns it on. While it is off, nothing is contaminated and Decontaminant is not used up. Next: put it all together with a steam plant feeding a Storage Ring.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.fuel_cell: Pipe hydrogen into the Hydrogen Fuel Cell and, if you can, oxygen too. Each unit of hydrogen gives 60 NE, spread over one second with oxygen fed. Without oxygen it breathes the air on a breathable world at half rate: the same 60 NE over twice the time. It puts out water; pipe it away so the tank never fills. Next: the Betavoltaic Cell.
gui.neropower.power_guide.step.betavolta: For power with no fuel line at all, a Betavoltaic Cell turns one Beta Capsule into a flat 4 NE/t for about 30 in-game days, with no heat and nothing to feed. A full buffer pauses the capsule instead of wasting it. When it is spent, vitrify the Spent Beta Capsule. Next: the Steam Plant.
